prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit with identity preservation.
Make one narrow correction to reference image 4. Output one 1536x1024 finished illustration.

References in exact order: image 1 is Demir's canonical identity, image 2 is Mirza's canonical identity, image 3 is the Bridge room master, and image 4 is the already repaired composition to edit.

PRESERVE the entire left side and character staging from image 4: identical Demir face, hair, expression, seated body, two visible arm chains, keyboard hand, mouse hand, desk and chair. Preserve Mirza's face, serious reaction, posture, two notebook grips, uniform and notebook. Preserve the lighting, colors and Bridge background.

Change only the large monitor assembly on the right and the alignment of its contents. Swivel its mount so the WHOLE PHYSICAL FRONT PANEL is completely frontal and exactly parallel to the camera sensor. The monitor front bezel and glass are true rectangles. Top and bottom edges are level horizontal lines. Left and right edges are exactly vertical. Opposite edges are parallel. Nothing on the front panel is trapezoidal or obliquely tilted. Use approximately x=805 to 1515 and y=130 to 750 for the rectangular front, with generous inner margins. Show a plausible swivel pedestal or stand beneath it that supports this frontal orientation.

The glass, bezel, title, title rule, five diagram boxes, arrows, footer rule and all text must now share this one front-facing rectangular plane. Every horizontal box edge and every text baseline is exactly level. Every vertical box edge is exactly vertical. Keep the five component labels large, crisp and readable at 768x512. Keep room materials and screen glow consistent.

Exact display text:
"Mission pipeline"
"Preprocessor"
"FFT extractor"
"Classifier"
"Anomaly detector"
"Reporter"
"Pulse interval: 47.0 s"

Exactly five component boxes and the same source-correct topology: Preprocessor connects to FFT extractor. FFT extractor branches to Classifier above and Anomaly detector below. Both parallel branches separately converge into Reporter. Clear arrowheads, no shortcuts, no extra components. Title and pulse interval stay outside the component boxes. Do not add completion status or new text.

Preserve every repaired hand and face from image 4. No pointer or new gesture. The only correction is the monitor's frontal geometry and its matching diagram plane.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: one finished 1536x1024 landscape story illustration for the System Architecture briefing in Tensorcraft's Deep Orbit course.

Reference roles, in this exact order:
1. Ensign Demir's canonical neutral portrait is the identity authority for Demir.
2. Commander Mirza's canonical neutral portrait is the identity authority for Mirza.
3. The Bridge master is the room and materials reference.
4. The existing briefing is the edit target. Preserve its warm green/brass palette, two-character briefing, large readable Mission pipeline display, correct diagram and 47.0 s. Rebuild the complete character staging and arm poses.

Scene: on the Archimedes Bridge, Demir has just opened the proposed five-component architecture on a large shared upright monitor. He sits at a normal desk console, operating a keyboard with his left hand and a mouse with his right hand. Both hands, wrists, forearms, elbows and shoulders must be plainly traceable in front of his own torso. Give the two forearms separate unobstructed silhouettes. Remove the pointer entirely. His elbows must not disappear behind Mirza. Let him lean slightly forward, showing engaged concentration and a small questioning lift of the brow while looking toward the shared diagram.

Mirza stands beside him with a clear gap from his arms and chair. She holds a closed plain notebook naturally against her lower torso with both hands, elbows resting beside her own body. Her arms never reach around Demir, never cross his silhouette and never pass behind his working arms. Her restrained, serious reaction to the shrinking pulse interval is visible in her raised inner brow, attentive eyes and slightly pressed mouth. She looks at the diagram and 47.0 s, not at the audience. Keep natural adult body/head proportions, supported seating and clearance under the desk. Both faces must be recognizable three-quarter views with readable light. Preserve Demir's facial width, jaw, nose, brown eyes, freckles, stubble, swept hair and left-ear device from portrait 1. Preserve Mirza's mature dark complexion, broad facial structure, nose, short silver-templed hair, age lines and charcoal/gold command uniform with a plain round chronometer from portrait 2.

Composition: candid medium-wide view beside the operators. Use the right half and available upper space for the large working monitor, with faces and all four hands clearly visible in the remaining space. The display faces the crew and is also readable from the camera. Keep all diagram text on the same perspective plane with generous margins, large crisp lettering readable at 768x512. Background bridge controls remain quiet and subordinate. No unnecessary small text.

Display text, exactly:
"Mission pipeline"
"Preprocessor"
"FFT extractor"
"Classifier"
"Anomaly detector"
"Reporter"
"Pulse interval: 47.0 s"

Exactly five component boxes. Preprocessor connects to FFT extractor. FFT extractor branches into two distinct parallel boxes: Classifier above and Anomaly detector below. Both branches separately converge into Reporter. Use clear arrowheads and generous spacing, with no direct shortcut and no extra sixth component. The title and pulse interval are plain heading/footer text, not component boxes. This is a proposed architecture, so do not add success checks, completed status or invented results.

Hands and objects: ordinary relaxed keyboard and mouse contacts, simple closed-notebook grips, five plausible digits per hand, normal thumb sides, aligned wrists and unbroken shoulder-elbow-wrist chains. No pointer, pen, open-palm gesture, crossing arms, duplicated limbs or hidden reconstruction of an elbow. Preserve the warm room atmosphere and specific interaction.
